title: Download many files from a list of URLs with curl and retries
summary: Reads a text file that has one web address per line and downloads each file into a folder. Temporary failures are retried a few times, and each address that still fails is reported, so you can run the list again for it.

steps.explain: Dry run: print the address that each line would download. This reads the list only and downloads nothing.
steps.cmd: while IFS= read -r url; do echo "would download: $url"; done < "<LIST_FILE>"
steps.expect: One line per address, such as: would download: https://example.org/a.pdf

placeholders.name: LIST_FILE
placeholders.description: Text file with one URL per line

steps.explain: Download every address into the output folder. -f treats HTTP errors as failures, --retry repeats temporary failures three times, and -O keeps the name from the URL. A failed address prints FAILED.
steps.cmd: (mkdir -p "<OUT_DIR>" && cd "<OUT_DIR>" && while IFS= read -r url; do curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 -O "$url" || echo "FAILED: $url"; done) < "<LIST_FILE>"
steps.expect: No output for files that downloaded; FAILED: followed by the address for the ones that did not.

placeholders.name: LIST_FILE
placeholders.description: Text file with one URL per line

placeholders.name: OUT_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder for the downloaded files; created if missing

steps.expect: One file per successful address, with its size.

prerequisites: A text file with one web address per line
warnings: -O takes the file name from the URL, so two addresses that end in the same name overwrite each other.
Retries happen only for temporary errors; a 404 is reported as FAILED at once.
Only download files you are allowed to use.
